mstts:express-as.prosody: Chapter Eight: The Wisdom of Suffering—What Illness Teaches. Suffering never asks permission. When it shows up, it’s never on your terms. It crashes in, shakes everything up, and leaves you feeling exposed. But as the weeks and months of illness unfold, something unexpected happens. All that pain, the fear, the constant uncertainty—they start peeling away what doesn’t really matter. Suddenly, there’s no energy left for pretending. The masks you used to wear? They just don’t fit anymore. And in this raw, honest place, the world seems to shift. The simplest things—a sunrise, someone’s voice on the phone, the taste of soup on a hard day—they become these tiny bursts of joy you probably missed before. It’s almost as if illness sharpens your senses, tuning you in to life’s quiet, beautiful details. Relationships change, too. The people who stick around, who check in and show up when it’s tough—they become your anchors. You realize there’s a new kind of honesty in these connections. Suddenly it’s okay to say you’re scared, or to ask for help, or just admit you don’t have it all together. The walls that used to separate you from others—they start to crumble. What’s left is this deep sense of shared humanity. And you gain a whole new understanding of what it means to care. If you’ve ever sat on both sides of a hospital bed, you know the difference between sympathy and empathy. It isn’t about quick fixes or easy words. What really matters is just being there—willing to sit with someone in their pain, to let them know, “Hey, I’m right here. You’re not alone.” The wisdom that grows from suffering isn’t something you can read about or hear in a lecture. It’s hard-won—earned through experience. You learn that life is unpredictable, that the idea of control is a bit of a mirage, and that love, for all its fragility, is also incredibly strong. And maybe, most of all, you discover that meaning isn’t something you stumble upon. It’s something you create. Moment by moment, with every choice you make.
